chunks: I said to Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: "A man begins the sa'i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and the time of salat enters. Should he shorten it, or perform salat and then return, or remain as he is until he finishes?"
So he عليه السلام said: "Is there not a mosque for him by them both? No; rather, he should perform salat and then return."
I said: "And may he sit on al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?" He عليه السلام said: "Yes."

key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: a place of prayer or mosque
key_terms.وَقْتُ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: the appointed time for ritual prayer
key_terms.ٱلسَّعْيِ: the ritual walking between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.ٱلصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two stations of sa'i
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other station of sa'i

ai.seo_question: If the time of prayer begins during sa'i between Safa and Marwah, should one stop and pray first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one performing sa'i when the time of salat begins. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that he should stop to perform salat and then return to complete the sa'i, and he also permits sitting on al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A man starts performing Sa'i (ritual walking) between Safa and Marwah, and the time for prayer begins. Should he hasten to complete it, or should he pray first and then return to complete it, or should he remain in his current state until he finishes?"
Imam (as) replied: "Isn't there a mosque between the two (Safa and Marwah)? No, rather he should pray first and then return to complete it."
I asked: "And can he sit on Safa and Marwah?" Imam (as) replied: "Yes."
